subject: design-technology
title: Digital Twins
welcome_lead: A live virtual copy of the physical asset — synchronised by sensor data.
meta_desc: A-Level D&T: digital twins in design and operation.
final_note: What you can model, you can predict.

concepts.def: Live virtual model of a physical asset, synced by sensor data.
Computational representation of a system's behaviour.
Real-time data stream from the physical asset to its twin.
Running scenarios on the twin to forecast outcomes.
Twin of a single physical item (e.g. a turbine).
Twin of a whole system (factory, city).

walkthroughs.body_html: The digital twin concept was articulated by Michael Grieves around 2002 and grew with cheap sensors and cloud compute. NASA used twin spacecraft on the ground during Apollo missions — an analogue ancestor.
Rolls-Royce monitors every Trent engine through a digital twin, using live sensor data to schedule maintenance and optimise fuel burn. Siemens twins entire factories before they are built.
A twin is only as good as its model and data. Garbage in, garbage out applies. Twins also raise cybersecurity concerns — they expose detailed system data.
